chapter: Early bands and joining George Lewis
title: Joining George Lewis and the road to national fame
summary: Drag recommended him to George Lewis. They played Manny's, got Nick as manager, moved to El Morocco (c. 1949-50), and Reverend Kershaw and Dr. Ball took them to Cincinnati, Los Angeles and beyond.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And we had a crippled fellow on the clarinet. I can't think of his name now. He's dead. And sometimes we have George Lewis and drag. Well, the piano player, I didn't know his name. Then we had another fellow by the name of Alfred used to play sax with us sometime when we couldn't get clarinet. Well, how I come to get into the George Lewis band, I played with Eddie Morris back at Linfans, back on Canal Boulevard. One Sunday afternoon. And George had a job at the corner from Drag's house. And he needed a drummer. So Drag told him about me, he said, well, go get him. He said, cause he's a good drummer. So Drag came and got me that night, left wood over at the house for a minute. So I went on a dead job with him that night. And the following week he had an advertisement for a prize fight. And he wanted to know if I could play that with him. I told him, yeah. So I played that with him, that night with him. And on the truck in the meantime he said, Joe, you playing with anybody regularly? I said, no, nobody but you all. He said, well, how would you like to work with me? He said, be able to make some good change. I said, sure. I said, I'll play with you until you can do better. Get somebody better, you know. Cause I didn't want him to think I was trying to be a hog or anything like that. So he said, alright. He said, you stick with me. He said, you're going to make it. He said, cause I like your style of playing. So you're playing that old time way. I said, well, alright. Well, we finally landed a job back on Benefit and St. Rock at Manny's. We played back there Friday and Saturday nights every week until the band started getting popular. And then we, Nick taking a liking to the band and he wanted to manage us. So George accepted him. And we went on out to El Moraca. That was around 1949 or 50, something like that. So from the El Moraca, that's where we started getting our breaks. Reverend Kershaw and Dr. Ball from Cincinnati. Where Reverend Kershaw was from Oxford. He had his church, Episcopal Church up there. And Dr. Ball was a professor at the University of Cincinnati. And they came down and they checked all the bands and they selected our band, the best one. So they started us to coming up into Cincinnati. And from Cincinnati, we started going out to Los Angeles. From Los Angeles, we started going into Frisco. And after that, we started going to several different states.
